newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil ticks up on low refinery offerings.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil ticks up on low refinery offerings.

text.p: Euro high sulphur fuel oil barges rose for the third day this week on Wednesday with low refinery offerings of prompt material cited as the main force behind the unseasonally high prices, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $96.50 and $96.75 fob ARA -- or some 75 cents a tonne up on Tuesday. Late offers rose to $98 for prompt material and $97 for loadings after August 11th.
Demand however was said to be moderate, some 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes, traders said.
"The refiners are still not offering and there are 20-hour delays in loadings," one trader said.
"The barges seem to be driving the whole market up," a second trader said.
Low sulphur barges were steady to a little stronger with some sellers at $96 and others $1 higher but little buying interest was seen.

"We were expecting low sulphur barges to go up sharply in line with the whole market but that is not happening and now you have low sulphur and high sulphur at about the same level...Demand is very low," one Rotterdam-based seller said.
High sulphur cargoes remain strong, notionally assessed around the $85 fob mark.
But no fresh deals were heard early after at least one deal on Tuesday at that figure.
"Not much has been going on so far today. Cargoes are around the same levels as Tuesday," one trader said.
Russian high sulphur straight continues to draw strong premiums, traders said.
